title: Workplace onboarding and safety basics
summary: A first-week course for new employees of any organization: the handbook and policies, where to get help, and the safety habits everyone on site follows. Add your own policies and site rules to each lesson.
overview: A starter course written by Resgrid in plain language for businesses and other employers. Your own policies, your site rules and the law where you operate come first: add them to each lesson before you publish the course.

lessons.title: Policies and the handbook
lessons.html:
Your employer's handbook explains how work is done here: hours, conduct, leave, equipment and how to raise a concern.

  • Read the handbook in your first week.
  • Acknowledge it when you are asked to, and again when it changes.
  • Ask your supervisor when something is not clear.

Add a link to your handbook and the policies new employees must read.

lessons.title: Where to get help
lessons.html:
Know who to call before you need them.

  • Your supervisor and their deputy.
  • Human resources, for questions about pay, leave and conduct.
  • The first aiders and the safety contact for your site.

lessons.title: Hazards and protective equipment
lessons.html:
A hazard is anything that could hurt someone. Look for them before you start a task.

  • Wear the protective equipment your task and area require.
  • Use only the equipment you have been trained and authorized to use.
  • Stop and report a hazard you cannot make safe yourself.

lessons.title: Emergencies and reporting
lessons.html:
Learn the evacuation signal, the nearest exits and the assembly point on your first day.

  • Report every injury, illness and near miss to your supervisor before the end of the shift.
  • A near miss is a warning: reporting it helps prevent the next injury.

questions.text: What should you do with a hazard you cannot make safe yourself?
options: Leave it for the next shift
questions.explanation: Stop and report a hazard you cannot make safe yourself.

questions.text: A near miss does not need to be reported because no one was hurt.
questions.explanation: Report near misses too: they show where the next injury could happen.

questions.text: When should you learn the evacuation signal and the assembly point?
questions.explanation: Learn the evacuation signal, the nearest exits and the assembly point on your first day.
